From: Oliver Grant <oliver@healthsync.co>

Cc: DPO Team <dpo@healthsync.co>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Passporting of dataflows / subprocessor snapshot request

Hi Mateo,

We're moving towards production with HealthSync's EU-only deployment, and legal asked me to get a clear picture of any transient cross-border movements that might occur when we rely on Redwood's hosted inference. A couple of concrete asks: 

- Can you provide a recent snapshot of subprocessors that may touch HealthSync data for inference, analytics, caching, or telemetry (APAC/EU/US split)?
- Do any of Redwood's default failover or autoscale behaviors allow ephemeral egress of customer data for up to 72 hours (we've heard of 48–72h windows for cache/KV syncs)? If so, what processors/regions are involved and how are they logged/audited?
- We're especially worried about embedding/PII pipelines — if embeddings or KV caches are involved, will they ever be routed outside the EU without explicit consent or a DPA amendment?

If you can attach a subprocessor CSV and a short statement on the transient-egress policy, that will help our DPO team triage. Also, if there's a draft DPA amendment you can share that enumerates the temporary-egress guardrails, please send that along.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Infrastructure
HealthSync

Attachments: (none yet)
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@healthsync.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Passporting of dataflows / subprocessor snapshot request

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Laura (product/compliance) and Kim (ops) so we can give you a single package. High level up-front: 

- Redwood supports region pinning (US / EU / APAC) at the account level. For HealthSync we've noted EU affinity in your onboarding. Under normal operations, inference calls, embeddings, and KV caches for pinned requests remain in-region.

- Temporary/ephemeral egress can occur only under two scenarios: (1) pre-authorized short failover windows (we call them transient-elevations) to maintain availability when a primary region is unhealthy, or (2) customer-configured cross-region analytics exports. The failover windows are configurable; our standard operational playbook allows a bounded 72-hour remediation window in extreme outages if the customer has not chosen Dedicated/Private.

- When transient-elevations occur, we prefer replication to a nearby region within the same legal territory (EU -> EU). If cross-territory routing is necessary (very rare), it is restricted to a small set of subprocessors listed in the attached CSV and is logged in our audit pipeline with per-request KMS-wrapped keys and telemetry blinding.

I attached three documents: a current subprocessor snapshot (CSV), a draft DPA amendment that includes a transient-egress clause, and an ops runbook describing our short-window replication controls. Please find them attached.

Quick asks for your team so we can tighten our response: 
- Confirm whether HealthSync will use the hosted multi-tenant endpoint or a Dedicated pool (Dedicated eliminates transient cross-territory egress by design).
- Expected peak token and request rate (helps us advise on autoscale policies).

If you're free, I can schedule a 30-min call Monday to walk through the CSV and the amendment.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Product Manager, Residency & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: healthsync_subprocessor_snapshot.csv (CSV), rdw_dpa_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF), ops-runbook-temporary-egress.md (MD)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@healthsync.co>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@healthsync.co>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Passporting of dataflows / subprocessor snapshot request

Mateo — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of clarifications from our side after a rapid scan: 

- HealthSync will be on the hosted endpoint initially; we expect to request Dedicated near EOY depending on cost/usage. So transient-elevations remain material for the moment.
- We process embeddings that contain hashed PII (patient identifiers pseudonymized upstream). Peak is roughly 150–250 req/s for embeddings during business hours; average token count per request is ~1k tokens. We expect burst scaling during launches up to ~400 req/s for short windows.

Questions: 
1) The CSV lists a small set of audit/analytics providers in the US and APAC that appear to receive telemetry and batched logs. Does telemetry ever include hashed embeddings or KV cache material that could be reverse-engineered? If so, is it pseudonymized/encrypted at rest and in transit?
2) For the DPA amendment, can you add an express clause that requires Redwood to notify HealthSync within 4 hours when any transient-elevation triggers cross-territory replication (and provide the affected request/trace ids)? Our legal team wants real-time visibility.

Can you confirm these points in writing so we can pass them to legal for an expedited review? If you prefer, we can take the call later today.

Thanks,
Oliver

Oliver — short answers & next steps: 

1) Telemetry and logs: We do not send unhashed or raw embedding payloads to third-party telemetry processors. Batched telemetry contains metadata (request ids, latency, error codes) and aggregate metrics. If you elect to enable application-level tracing, we can pseudonymize trace metadata server-side and ensure embeddings are never stored in plain telemetry. All telemetry is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest; select telemetry tables have field-level encryption and are KMS-wrapped. 

2) 4-hour notification SLA for cross-territory transient-elevations: we can add an express notification clause to the DPA amendment. Proposed language: "Redwood will notify Customer within four (4) hours of any activation of cross-territory transient-elevation and provide the associated request trace ids and affected subprocessor roster for the event." Marissa will redline the exact placement, but we can commit to the operational 4-hour timeline in DocuSign if HealthSync is comfortable.

Next steps / commitments: 
- Marissa/legal will run through the DPA amendment and send a redline by EOD Wednesday.
- Ops will produce a short CSV with the subset of subprocessors we might use for extreme cross-territory failover (attached today).
- I'll schedule a 30-min call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to walk these items with your DPO — meeting invite attached.

If Hosted proves operationally insufficient, Dedicated is the fastest path to eliminate cross-territory exposure; we can provide a pricing delta and migration runbook.

Thanks — we should have Marissa's redline shortly.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Product Manager, Residency & Compliance
Redwood Inference
